reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with an Iterator over two known items, alpha and beta, and a valid one-second Delay on its loop path.
On the Iterator completed branch, add a Delay whose Seconds uses Current Item Index. Explicitly commit the variable selection and verify the saved configuration.
Test the workflow and confirm successful completion with final Iterator result currentItemIndex 2 and hasProcessedAllItems true.
Inspect the completed-branch Delay’s Input tab and expand Iterator. Observe alpha, index 0 and false, including the consumed index highlighted as 0.
Compare the successful execution and stored final Iterator result; do not count an uncommitted variable or zero-duration execution failure as this display defect.
bugs.sourceCause: The Input inspector passes no selected loop index for a step outside the loop. Its context helper defaults to history index 0 of an array containing historical results before the latest result. Backend execution instead uses each step’s current result.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Covers stale completed-branch Input context only. Delay variable selection not saving (workflows-pass2-7b30d0b9) and zero-duration execution failure (workflows-fresh-a4320e8f) remain existing coverage. Node-tab configuration interpretation, nested Input crashes and skipped-iteration Output gating are different claims.

reviewEvidence.basis: Independent browser controls and source verification, followed by separate own-session reviews explicitly grading the original narrow Input-display claim; both accepted at severity 1. Coordinator checked source, subscription billing and retained successful-run/Input/Node screenshots.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The run inspector misreports context while execution and stored results remain correct.
limitations: Observed impact is misleading inspection information; execution and stored final Iterator results are correct when the Delay variable is committed.
Original execution failures are already covered by the Delay variable-save and zero-duration references and contribute no severity to this entry.
The claim concerns the Input tab, not the Node tab showing stored configuration or an inside-loop selected historical iteration.
Other completed-branch action types and nested Iterator scope were not browser-established.
The unintended history-index fallback is inferred from documentation, source and passing execution controls; no maintainer acknowledgement of this exact display bug was found.
Newer source retains the relevant history selection; newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: Workflow Form submits a previous valid date while displaying an incomplete replacement
bugs.summary: Editing a previously valid Form Date to an impossible or incomplete date leaves that new text visible, but Submit silently stores the previous valid date as the answer.
bugs.expected: Submitting a Form should represent the displayed response, or visibly reject or revert an incomplete edit before submitting a different value.
bugs.actual: After entering 11/12/2026, replacing it with 02/30/2026 leaves 02/30/202_ visible without an error. Dismissing the calendar and clicking Submit completes the run with the stale 2026-11-12 response, which remains after reload.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with a Form containing one Date input. Test the saved workflow.
Enter a valid date such as 11/12/2026 and click the Form title to close the calendar.
Replace the date with 02/30/2026. Observe the incomplete 02/30/202_ text and no explanatory validation message.
Click outside to close the calendar, then click Submit. Inspect the completed Form Output and persisted run state; the prior valid 2026-11-12 is submitted.

Control: replace the original date with a valid new date and verify that new answer submits. An invalid date entered into an initially empty optional field should be distinguished from this stale-previous-answer claim.
bugs.sourceCause: The date mask calls its parent only on completion. An incomplete replacement remains locally visible without updating the Form value or error state. The Form submits its retained previous value, which the server stores as the response.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Shares the completion-only date-input pattern with keyboard-clearing a saved workflow date, but this entry covers Form filling and a completed stored stale answer. Rejected N58 explicitly excludes stale-previous-date submission; open-calendar first-click dismissal and invalid local workflow configuration are separate claims.

reviewEvidence.basis: Independent browser/source verification with two stale-response repetitions per reviewer, valid-date and initially-empty controls, submitted-response and stored-result checks; coordinator inspected both reviewers’ invalid-input/output screenshots and audited pinned/latest source.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The completed run stores a different date from the visible edited answer.
limitations: The calendar was deliberately dismissed before Submit; this is not a first click consumed by an open popup.
No downstream record creation or external action was tested; observed impact is the persisted incorrect Form response.
An invalid answer entered into an initially empty optional Date field submits no value and is not this defect.
Other date-input callers and roles are not established runtime scope.
Newer source retains the relevant completion-only path; newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: Group by None does not clear Workflow Runs relation grouping even after reload
bugs.summary: Choosing None in a Workflow Runs Table grouped by Workflow version or Workflow leaves the saved relation grouping intact across reload.
bugs.expected: The supported Group by None action should remove the selected grouping, including when a relation grouping currently has no configured groups.
bugs.actual: None closes the menu but Workflow version or Workflow remains selected. The saved view retains that grouping field and reload does not clear it. Switching first to Workflow run status and then None successfully clears grouping after reload.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Workflow Runs Table view and choose Group by Workflow version. Leave its relation groups unconfigured.
Choose Group by None, reopen Options and observe the previous grouping still selected.
Reload the same view and verify the relation grouping remains selected.
Repeat on a fresh view or with Workflow relation grouping.
Control: switch to Workflow run status grouping, then None. Confirm the saved grouping clears after reload, distinguishing a persistent no-op from the separate transient stale-page problem.
bugs.sourceCause: The reset handler returns early when the saved viewGroups array is empty. Workflow and Workflow version are nonnullable relation fields that can legitimately have a selected grouping with no generated groups, so the clearing mutation is never reached.

matchingGuidance.distinction: The existing Opportunities/Tasks reference saves null successfully and only leaves the open page stale until reload. This entry covers Workflow Runs nonnullable relations whose empty group list makes None skip saving, so reload still retains grouping. The older Workflow Versions/status reference is a different collection/field and does not establish the cause or persistent-reload scope; no claim about its reload recovery is made.

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent reviewers reproduced persistent None removal failure on two fresh Workflow Runs views with relation and select-field controls, then verified source and explicit maintainer repair. Coordinator checked billing, saved-view identities/readbacks, retained screenshots and the captured Codex recording.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: An offered grouping-removal action does not remove the saved grouping; switching through a select field is required as a workaround.
limitations: No workflow run records were lost or changed.
Missing automatically populated relation groups is intentional and is not the proposed defect; failure of the explicit None action is.
The select-field control clears saved grouping even if the open page remains stale before reload; that transient display issue is existing coverage.
The absence of a clearing request is inferred from the early return and unchanged saved state, not a reliable request-interception trace.
One reviewer’s retained recording is truncated; retained screenshots and saved-state readbacks plus the other reviewer’s complete captured recording substantiate the checks.
Newer source contains a guard/state correction; newer runtime and branch chronology were not tested or inferred.

bugs.name: Workflow Run Flow diagrams stay clipped after navigation or viewport size changes
bugs.summary: The full Workflow Run Flow page keeps an obsolete horizontal diagram position after a tablet navigation drawer is collapsed or a 768px run page narrows to 390px, clipping step labels and completion marks.
bugs.expected: The run diagram should remain readable when its visible container size changes, as it does when loaded directly at the same final width.
bugs.actual: Opening a completed run behind expanded tablet navigation and collapsing it leaves both nodes partly beyond the left edge. Separately, resizing a correctly displayed 768px full run page to 390px leaves nodes beyond the right edge. The run remains completed; reload with navigation closed or normal canvas panning restores readability.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with a Search Records step and complete a run. Open its preview at 768px with navigation expanded, then Open the full run page.
Collapse navigation and inspect Flow. The left portions of the trigger and action labels are clipped. Control: load the same run at 768px with navigation already collapsed; labels fit.
Independent variant: load a completed full run Flow page at 768px with readable nodes, then narrow the viewport to 390px without reloading.
Observe nodes extend beyond the right canvas edge, clipping labels and success marks. Opening and closing the command menu after this resize does not restore readability.
Reload at 390px with navigation closed, or pan the canvas. The complete nodes and marks become readable. Repeat using fresh runs/workflows.
bugs.sourceCause: The shared diagram base calculates horizontal centering from its container offsetWidth during initialization and selected panel transitions. It does not recenter in response to container-width changes. A zero-width container behind expanded navigation yields a left offset, while later viewport narrowing retains an oversized-width offset.

matchingGuidance.relatedReferenceName: Resizing the workflow editor to mobile hides the graph until reload
matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry covers the full Workflow Run Flow record page and two variants of its stale container-size centering: tablet navigation collapse and 768→390 viewport resize. The related entry covers the editable workflow graph. Both opposite-direction clipping reports are one canonical full-run defect. Exclude execution failure, data loss and independently unconfirmed menu-only/no-resize variants.

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent reviewers verified both trigger variants at GUI severity 1. Coordinator checked all four final reports, source/history/coverage, actual original Mo video frames, independent clipped/reloaded screenshots, retained recording files and subscription billing. Direct-load, desktop, reload and normal-pan controls recover readable nodes.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Diagram presentation is clipped; execution state is correct and panning/reload restores readability.
limitations: Only the full run Flow page and short manual/Search Records graphs are jointly established; additional roles, long graphs and other graph surfaces are not added.
No workflow execution or stored configuration loss was observed.
Menu-only clipping without a preceding resize was an extra non-joint variation and is excluded.
Newer centering arithmetic changed but retains size-response concerns in source; newer runtime was not tested.
The exact hidden-container measurement and mount ordering are source-backed inferences supported by observed offsets and controls; no full layout lifecycle trace was captured.

bugs.name: A valid Number answer bypasses another workflow Form field’s validation
bugs.summary: Entering a valid answer in one Number field re-enables workflow Form submission while another field still displays invalid text and its validation error.
bugs.expected: Submit should remain disabled while any Number answer has a validation error. Correcting another field must not clear the invalid field’s submission gate.
bugs.actual: With two uniquely named Number fields, entering abc in the first disables Submit. Entering 42 in the second re-enables Submit while abc and Invalid number remain. Submission completes with only the second answer. If the first previously held a valid number, submission instead retains that previous value behind the invalid replacement text.
reproSteps: Create and activate a saved manual workflow with a Form containing two Number fields with distinct labels, such as Alpha and Beta.
Start a fresh run and enter abc in Alpha. Confirm Invalid number is displayed and Submit is disabled.
Enter 42 in Beta without correcting Alpha. Observe Submit becomes usable while Alpha still shows abc and its error.
Submit and inspect the completed Form result: Beta is 42 and Alpha is omitted. Repeat in another fresh run.
Stale-answer variation: enter a valid Alpha value first, replace it with invalid text, then enter a valid Beta value and submit. The completed result retains the prior valid Alpha value.
Control: correct Alpha to a valid number and submit both valid answers; both appear correctly in the completed result.
bugs.sourceCause: The Form filler uses one shared error value for all fields. A valid Number field calls the shared error callback with undefined, overwriting another field’s error and enabling Submit. Invalid text remains local to its input and does not update the stored answer, so submission omits it or sends the previous valid number.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Match runtime Number-field validation bypass caused by editing a valid sibling Number field. The stale Date-answer and untouched Select-default entries have different input-adapter causes. Exclude invalid workflow configuration, duplicate form labels, and claims that raw invalid text is stored.

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent reviewers reproduced the bypass in two fresh executions of saved, activated workflows and observed completed results omitting the invalid answer. Both also confirmed stale previous-number submission and passing valid-answer controls. Coordinator checked original visual evidence, independent screenshots and retained recordings, actual submitted-result readbacks, subscription billing, source, and the explicit submission-blocking maintainer contract.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The runtime validation gate is bypassed and completed Form results disagree with the displayed answers.
limitations: Raw invalid text is not stored; the observed result omits the answer or uses its previous valid parsed value.
Each reviewer repeated fresh executions of its own saved workflow; two independent workflow configurations per reviewer are not claimed.
No downstream record, email or other action consequences were tested.
Other roles and AI-form runtime behavior are not established.
The inspected newer workflow Form source retains shared error tracking; newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: HTTP body property content-type receives header validation and is omitted on save
bugs.summary: A newly entered content-type property in an HTTP Request Key/Value body is incorrectly treated as a reserved header and omitted from saved body configuration.
bugs.expected: Body property names should be validated as payload properties, independently of restrictions on manually entered HTTP headers.
bugs.actual: Entering content-type=document under Body Input > Key/Value shows “This key should be set through body input.” After reload the property is absent, while an ordinary body property remains. Raw JSON preserves a content-type property.
reproSteps: Create a fresh manual workflow and add an HTTP Request action using POST.
Set Body Input to Key/Value. Enter an ordinary property such as title=document and allow saving.
Add a body property content-type=document. Observe the red header-oriented validation message beneath its name.
Wait, reload and reopen the action. Observe that the ordinary property remains but content-type is absent.
Repeat on another fresh workflow. Control: a Raw JSON body containing a content-type property survives save and reload.
bugs.sourceCause: The shared KeyValuePairInput applies the reserved-header content-type guard to every caller and filters flagged rows from onChange. BodyInput reuses that component without a header-only switch, so valid payload properties are filtered before the debounced body save.

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent reviewers reproduced the body-key validation error and missing reloaded Key/Value property with fresh workflow data and ordinary-key/Raw JSON controls. Coordinator checked complete reports, original and independent visual evidence, retained recordings, source and contract audits, and subscription billing.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Normal editing cannot save the valid body property through the affected path. Both reviewers recommend severity 3.
limitations: This covers newly entered properties, not erasure of a previously acknowledged saved body field.
Both reviewers also observed the error in Form Data; saved Form Data omission was independently established by only one reviewer and is not added to the joint claim.
A reviewer found an edit/delete bypass that can save the key; the claim is the normal editing path, not universal inability to store it.
No request execution or downstream server damage was tested.
Unintended body-side validation is inferred from the separate payload/header contract, controls and shared-component history. Newer source was inspected, not run.

bugs.name: Deleting another HTTP header saves and locks a rejected Content-Type header
bugs.summary: Deleting an unrelated header saves a manually entered Content-Type header that normal editing rejects, then reload turns it into a disabled managed row.
bugs.expected: Deleting another row must preserve the same reserved-header validation as ordinary editing and must not save a rejected header as an uneditable managed value.
bugs.actual: A GET action rejects Content-Type=text/plain with “This key should be set through body input.” Deleting X-Temporary causes Content-Type to persist. After reload the warning disappears and its key, value and trash button are disabled. Without the deletion, only X-Temporary persists.
reproSteps: Create a fresh manual workflow and add an HTTP Request action using GET.
In Headers Input enter Content-Type=text/plain and observe the reserved-header validation warning.
Add X-Temporary=remove, wait normally, then delete only the X-Temporary row using its trash button.
Wait, reload and reopen the action. Observe that Content-Type=text/plain remains, its warning is gone and its key/value/delete controls are disabled.
Repeat with a fresh workflow. Control: reload the same rejected Content-Type plus ordinary X-Temporary setup without deleting a row; Content-Type is omitted and X-Temporary remains editable.
bugs.sourceCause: The edit reducer filters non-managed reserved keys, but the remove reducer serializes every remaining nonempty row without that validation. Reload classifies the saved reserved key as automatically managed, suppresses its warning and disables editing and deletion.

matchingGuidance.relatedReferenceName: HTTP body property content-type receives header validation and is omitted on save
matchingGuidance.distinction: The shared key/value component is involved in both entries. This entry covers deleting another Headers Input row and saving a rejected reserved header. The related entry covers normal Body Input editing incorrectly omitting a valid payload property; these opposite save paths are distinct triggers.

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent reviewers reproduced the GET-header deletion trigger twice with fresh workflows and passing no-deletion controls. Coordinator checked full reports, source and validation contract, original and independent visual evidence, actual browser readbacks, retained recordings and subscription billing.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: An unrelated row deletion saves rejected configuration and disables its ordinary correction after reload. Both reviewers recommend severity 3.
limitations: No request execution, outgoing header behavior or security impact was tested or inferred as observed damage.
Method/body-mode variations do not establish that deleting the step is the only possible recovery. Lowercase spelling has a tested method-change workaround.
Body-editor sibling variations share the reducer but are outside this narrowly defined GET-header reproduction.
The inspected newer source retains the reducer omission; newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: Workflow Update Record ignores a saved clear of Company revenue amount
bugs.summary: Clearing Annual Revenue Amount Micros saves a blank mapping, but a successful Update Record action retains the Company’s previous amount while applying the new currency.
bugs.expected: A selected amount explicitly cleared to null must clear the stored amount when Update Record executes.
bugs.actual: A Create Record action creates a Company with amountMicros 3210000/USD. Update Record configured with blank Amount Micros and EUR remains blank after reload, but execution returns 3210000/EUR and leaves that amount on the Company. Explicit 0/EUR correctly stores 0/EUR.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with Create Record for Companies, setting a unique name and Annual Revenue amountMicros 3210000/USD.
Add Update Record targeting the Company created by the first action and select Annual Revenue. Set Amount Micros to 0 and Currency Code to EUR. Wait for saving and test; confirm 0/EUR.
Clear only Amount Micros with Backspace or Delete, blur, wait for saving and reload. Reopen Update Record and confirm the amount is blank while EUR remains.
Test the saved workflow and inspect Update Record output and the created Company. The run succeeds but retains 3210000 while changing currency to EUR.
Repeat with a fresh workflow or a new duplicate whose record reference is explicitly remapped. Compare the passing explicit-zero control.
bugs.sourceCause: The workflow’s Update Record service runs the saved record mapping through removeUndefinedFromRecord before writing it. That helper uses isDefined and recursively removes null as well as undefined. The explicit amount clear is therefore omitted from the update, while the defined currency is retained.

matchingGuidance.relatedReferenceName: Create Record displays No Status but creates To do tasks and ignores explicitly selected No Status
matchingGuidance.distinction: The shared null-removal helper is involved, but this entry covers clearing an existing Company revenue amount through Update Record. The related entry covers Task status defaults and explicit No Status through Create Record. Do not match interrupted autosave, fractional micros validation, or client-side date clears that never save.

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent reviewers confirmed a saved blank Company Annual Revenue amount is ignored during successful Update Record execution, with passing explicit-zero controls. Coordinator checked full reports, source and clearing contract, original Mo samples, independent screenshots and sampled recordings, actual browser readbacks and subscription billing.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: A completed workflow silently fails to apply a saved field clear and leaves an incorrect stored amount. Both independent reviewers recommend severity 3.
limitations: Joint scope is Company Annual Revenue amount clearing in a manual Create Record → Update Record workflow. Other fields and callers are outside this entry.
One reviewer constructed an original workflow and duplicated/remapped a second; the other used two fresh workflows.
An interrupted original recording lacks a duration; retained screenshots and official browser readbacks support those controls. Complete recordings from both reviewers are not claimed.
The inspected newer source preserves null and adds clearing tests; newer runtime was not tested. No scheduled execution was tested.

bugs.name: Workflow Update Record ignores saved No Status and retains the Task’s previous status
bugs.summary: Update Record saves No Status correctly, but successful execution leaves the Task’s existing status unchanged.
bugs.expected: Selecting Status under Fields to update and explicitly choosing No Status must clear the Task status when the saved action executes.
bugs.actual: After No Status saves and survives reload, the workflow completes successfully but Update Record returns TODO or IN_PROGRESS inherited from Create Record. Selecting Done instead updates the status correctly.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with Create Record for Tasks, a unique title and To do status.
Add Update Record targeting the created Task. Select Status under Fields to update, choose Done, wait for saving and test; confirm the run completes and output status is DONE.
Choose No Status in Update Record, wait for saving and reload. Reopen the action and confirm No Status remains selected.
Test the saved workflow. The run completes, but Update Record output and the Task retain TODO.
Repeat with a fresh Task starting In progress and with only Status selected for update; the successful action retains IN_PROGRESS. Compare the passing Done control.
bugs.sourceCause: No Status emits null and the saved workflow retains that selected field value. Before writing the record, UpdateRecordService calls removeUndefinedFromRecord, whose isDefined guard removes null as well as undefined. Status is omitted from the update, so the previous stored value remains.

matchingGuidance.relatedReferenceName: Create Record displays No Status but creates To do tasks and ignores explicitly selected No Status
matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry covers Update Record clearing an existing Task status, which retains its previous value. N53 covers Create Record status defaults and explicit No Status. The related Company revenue entry covers composite amount clearing through Update Record. Do not match interrupted autosave or unsupported fractional-value normalization.

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent reviewers confirmed that a saved No Status selection is ignored during successful Task Update Record execution, with passing Done controls. Coordinator checked full reports, source and null-clearing contract, original and independent visual evidence, actual saved-mapping readbacks, sampled recordings and subscription billing.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: A successful workflow silently ignores a saved supported field clear, leaving the Task in the wrong status. Both independent reviewers recommend severity 3.
limitations: Joint scope is Task Status clearing through a saved Update Record action. Assignee and other fields are not covered by this entry.
One reviewer used one workflow with several fresh tasks; the other used two fresh workflows.
The ordinary record null-clear control used the application GraphQL API after its headless record dropdown did not open.
Broader null-valued update effects are source-supported but not established for every field; defined empty strings are not shown to fail.
The inspected newer source preserves null and adds clearing tests; newer runtime and activated launches were not tested.

bugs.name: Workflow Form date Clear leaves partial input visible when the answer was initially empty
bugs.summary: Clear closes the date picker but retains incomplete date text in an initially empty workflow Form input.
bugs.expected: The explicit Clear command should empty the displayed date input, including partial input.
bugs.actual: After entering an invalid or partial date in an initially empty Form Date field, clicking Clear closes the calendar but leaves text such as 02/30/202_ or 12/__/____ visible. Clearing a valid date empties the mask. Submitting the partial-input case still produces a null answer.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with a Form containing a Date field and test it with the date initially empty.
Enter 02/30/2026 so the masked input displays 02/30/202_. Open the calendar and click Clear.
Observe the calendar closes while the partial date remains visible. Repeat with partial input 12.
As a control, enter a valid date and click Clear; the input returns to its empty mask.
bugs.sourceCause: The date input keeps incomplete mask text locally and only notifies its parent for completed dates. Clear sets the already-null parent date to null. The mounted masked input resets only when its internal date differs from the parent date, so this unchanged-null clear does not erase the local partial text.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry requires the explicit Clear command on an initially empty Form Date field. It does not cover optional invalid-date validation without Clear, first-click popup dismissal, or submission of a previous valid date.

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent reviewers reproduced the same narrowed defect and passing control. Coordinator checked full reports, source/contract audits, original Mo video samples, independent screenshots or sampled recordings, executed browser readbacks and actual subscription billing.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The explicit Clear command leaves a misleading partial display; actual answer remains null.
limitations: Joint scope is workflow Form Date input. Other date and datetime callers are excluded.
This is a display defect: tested submission produces null, with no saved-answer loss.
The inspected newer source retains the reset guard; newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: Reconnecting a workflow edge onto an existing action opens unwanted action creation
bugs.summary: An existing edge reconnect saves correctly but also opens Select Action and overlays its destination with a temporary Add an Action node.
bugs.expected: Reconnecting an edge onto an existing node should update that connection without starting node creation.
bugs.actual: Dragging the arrow end of an existing connection onto an existing action saves the reconnect, but Select Action opens and a temporary Add an Action placeholder and edge cover the destination. Closing the panel or reloading restores the correct saved graph. A new connection onto an existing node does not open action creation.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with two existing actions and a connection to the first action.
Select the existing connection and drag its arrow end onto the second existing action.
Observe the reconnect succeeds while Select Action opens and a temporary Add an Action placeholder appears over the destination.
Close the panel or reload; the unwanted placeholder disappears and the intended connection remains. Compare a new connection between existing nodes, which opens no creation panel.
bugs.sourceCause: The reconnect drag records connection-start information used by drag-to-create. The ordinary connect handler clears it, while the reconnect path does not. The shared connect-end handler can therefore start node creation after reconnecting. Exact callback ordering is inferred from the source and observed controls.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Requires reconnecting an existing edge onto an existing action. Do not match intentional plus-button insertion, dragging a new connection onto empty canvas, or persistent malformed-loop execution defects.

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent reviewers reproduced the unwanted creation panel and temporary placeholder after reconnecting an existing edge, while ordinary new connections onto an existing node passed. Coordinator checked full reports, source and explicit upstream reconnect guard, original Mo samples, independent screenshots and controls, recorded artifacts and actual subscription billing.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The intended saved connection remains correct; the unwanted panel and temporary overlapping placeholder are a recoverable GUI defect. Both independent reviewers recommend severity 1.
limitations: Joint scope is reconnecting an existing edge onto an existing action in the editable workflow canvas, which opens temporary action creation despite saving the intended connection.
Closing the unwanted panel or reloading removes the temporary placeholder; no unintended extra saved action or execution failure is claimed.
The initial mistaken insert-button click and one reviewer’s later action selection are excluded.
Exact callback timing and behavior of the pinned graph-library version are inferred; the inspected newer source adds a reconnect guard, but newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: Rejected Workflow Run status drag leaves the card in the destination column
bugs.summary: A forbidden Workflow Run status change is rejected by the server, but Kanban retains the optimistic column placement until reload.
bugs.expected: After a rejected status drag, the run card should return to its saved status column.
bugs.actual: Dragging a Failed workflow run into Completed displays a permission error, but the card remains under Completed. Its badge can disagree with the column or retain the optimistic label. Reload returns the card to Failed; the stored status was not changed.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow that produces two Failed runs. Open Workflow Runs in a Kanban view grouped by run status.
Drag one owned Failed run into Completed and wait for the permission error.
Observe the card remains in Completed after the rejection and a settled wait. Repeat with the second failed run.
Reload and confirm both return to Failed. Compare an allowed Opportunity stage drag, which saves and remains in its destination after reload.
bugs.sourceCause: The board optimistically moves the record ID between column lists before updating the record. The run-update hook rejects status edits. Record field rollback does not restore the separately maintained board-column membership, so the rejected move remains visible.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry covers Workflow Runs and its run-update permission rejection. N04 covers Workflow Versions and its distinct version-status rejection. Do not match an actual saved status change, delayed execution, or a rejected delete banner.

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent reviewers reproduced two rejected failed-run drags leaving the card in Completed, with reload restoring Failed and a permitted Opportunity stage-drag control. Coordinator checked full reports, source and read-only run-status contract, original Mo video samples, independent screenshots and controls, and actual subscription billing.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The server preserves the correct status while the board displays a false placement until refresh. Both independent reviewers recommend GUI severity 1.
limitations: Joint scope is Workflow Runs Kanban status-column placement after a rejected Failed-to-Completed drag. No persisted run-status change or execution failure is claimed.
The badge varies between attempts and may show Failed or the optimistic destination status; the stable defect is placement in the wrong column.
Both reviewers used two failed runs in one owned workflow, rather than two independently constructed workflows.
Exact cache/mount ordering is inferred. Newer source adds drag restrictions to some dashboard and record-page relation widgets; no newer-runtime result is claimed.
Same-column reorder, other destinations, grouped-table/calendar callers and broader object behavior are excluded.

bugs.name: Reselecting a workflow condition field clears its saved comparison while displaying the old value
bugs.summary: Reselecting the current field can conceal an empty saved comparison and make a workflow Filter execute differently from its visible condition.
bugs.expected: The comparison shown in the editor should match the condition saved and executed after field reselection.
bugs.actual: After reselecting Workspace Member Id, the comparison input still shows the previous text or valid member ID, but the saved comparison is empty. Is can remain Is, leaving the panel visually unchanged. A Test then rejects the matching member and skips the downstream action. Reopening or reloading reveals the empty comparison.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow with Filter: Workspace Member Id Is the current member ID, followed by a Create Record action. Save and Test to verify the Filter passes and the action executes.
Open the Filter field picker and explicitly reselect the current Workspace Member Id field. Observe the same Is condition and member ID remain visible.
Wait for the edit to save and Test again. The saved flow uses an empty comparison, the Filter returns false and the downstream action is skipped.
Reopen the Filter or reload to reveal the empty comparison. Re-enter the member ID and Test to restore the passing result; merely opening and dismissing the picker preserves it.
bugs.sourceCause: Selecting the field writes the default operand and initial empty comparison. The string input initializes its editor from defaultValue only; its stable filter ID keeps the editor mounted without synchronizing cleared content. Execution reads the saved empty comparison.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry requires FIELD reselection, including reselecting the same field while Is remains Is. The related entry covers OPERATOR changes. Both can conceal a cleared saved comparison, but match the reported selector trigger. Do not require or infer a wrong If/Else branch from a stale input alone.

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent reviewers reproduced field reselection clearing the saved comparison while retaining its visible text, and each verified an incorrect Filter result against a valid workspace member with passing controls. Coordinator checked full reports, all source/contract audits, original Mo video samples, independent actual screenshots, owned saved/run readbacks and exact subscription billing.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Both independent reviewers observed a different Filter result and skipped downstream action despite a visible valid comparison, and recommend severity 3.
limitations: Joint scope is reselecting the current Workspace Member Id field in a Filter string condition, including Is remaining Is while its comparison is cleared. Operator-only changes are covered separately.

The visible stale comparison can cause a Filter to reject a member and skip its downstream action. If/Else stale-display observations are supplementary; an independently verified wrong If/Else branch is not claimed.
Fresh independent workflows and passing no-reselection, reopen/reload and re-entered-value controls support the issue. Other field types, roles and layouts are excluded.
The inspected newer source retains initialization-only editor content with the selector reset; newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.name: A stale schedule hour from valid typing is persisted by a later minute edit
bugs.summary: Typing a valid two-digit schedule hour can restore a stale prefix; editing only minutes then saves the wrong hour.
bugs.expected: A valid configured hour should remain consistent with the completed input, and editing minutes should preserve that hour.
bugs.actual: Fast entry of 23 can leave the hour field and preview at 2/02:00 even while a saved readback still holds 23. Changing only Minutes then saves hour 2 with the new minute. Reloading and reopening retains the wrong hour and preview.
reproSteps: Create a manual workflow, switch to a daily scheduled trigger, and configure an hour.
Replace the hour with 23 using fast ordinary typing; wait for saves. Repeat if needed until the field and preview show 2/02:00.
Change only Minutes, wait for the save, then reload and reopen the trigger. The hour remains 2 with the new minute.
Compare normal-speed entry, a one-digit hour edit, and retyping the intended hour; these controls preserve the intended setting.
bugs.sourceCause: Hour changes dispatch saves per keystroke. A completed response updates the flow using its captured submitted trigger, and the controlled input synchronizes to that echoed value. An older response can restore a stale prefix; the minute handler copies that stale hour into its next save. Exact server commit ordering is not independently traced.

matchingGuidance.distinction: This entry requires a VALID completed hour such as 23 reverting to a stale prefix and an ordinary later minute edit persisting that wrong hour. N52 and the invalid-minute prefix negative concern out-of-range input and do not establish a defect from rejected invalid input or prefix retention alone.

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent reviewers reproduced valid hour entry leaving a stale displayed hour, then a later minute-only edit persisting that wrong hour. Coordinator checked source/contract and preceding negative scopes, original evidence and independent actual browser readbacks/screenshots, natural timing provenance without injected responses, passing controls and exact subscription billing.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Both independent reviewers observed an unintended saved schedule hour after a valid edit and later minute-only change, and recommend severity 3.
limitations: Joint scope is valid hour typing that leaves stale hour 2 visible after entering 23, followed by an ordinary minute-only edit persisting hour 2 across reload/reopen.
Both reviewers support the later-minute propagation. Plain-reload-only wrong persistence was additionally observed by one reviewer; it is not required or claimed as independently reproduced by both.

The reviewed original browser calls used normal keyboard timing and observational request/response logging, with no response interception or injected delay. Repeated fast typing is timing-sensitive; observed frequencies are not production prevalence estimates.
Saved schedule and preview are affected. Actual scheduled execution, all Cron fields, decimal editing and sibling minute-digit loss are not in joint scope.
The inspected newer source changes trigger updates; no newer runtime success or precise server commit-order trace is claimed.

bugs.name: Tab traps focus in Delay duration inputs and leaves edits unsaved
bugs.summary: Typing a Delay duration and pressing Tab leaves focus in the same input, so its blur-based save never runs and reload restores the old duration.
bugs.expected: Tab moves focus out of an editable Delay duration input and allows the editor to commit the new value.
bugs.actual: After changing Seconds from 0 to 5 and pressing Tab, the field keeps focus and displays 5 without saving. Reloading and reopening the action shows 0. Repeated Tab and a wait do not commit it. Clicking another field or leaving through normal in-app navigation does save the edit.
reproSteps: Create a disposable workflow with a Delay action using After a set amount of time and a known saved duration. A deactivated workflow can demonstrate the failure.
Change Seconds, press Tab and inspect the focused input. Wait before reloading.
Reload the workflow and reopen Delay; compare the old duration. Repeat on a fresh workflow.
As a control, change the duration and click another field before reloading; verify that edit persists.
bugs.sourceCause: Delay stores duration edits locally and calls its action update only on blur. The number input uses TextInput hotkeys with no Tab callback. The default handler prevents the native Tab action, so focus stays in the input, blur never occurs and no duration update is submitted.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Match typed Delay duration edits followed by Tab that traps focus and leaves the value unsaved. Distinguish Delay variable-picker insert/remove loss, date-mask clearing, interrupted pending autosaves and execution failures. Deactivation is not required.
matchingGuidance.relatedReferenceName: Delay variable selection or removal stays local and is lost after ordinary panel navigation

reviewEvidence.basis: Both independent browser/source reviewers reproduce the Tab trap and duration reversion at severity 3 with working real-blur controls. Coordinator checked full reports, source/intent audits, independent retained original images and executed focus/save/readback controls, and exact subscription billing.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The editor displays a changed workflow duration without committing it through the expected Tab interaction; reload restores the old configuration.
limitations: Joint scope is Tab after editing Delay duration, with Seconds and Minutes checks. Days/Hours, other callers and roles are not independently established affected.
Real mouse blur, panel departure and ordinary in-app navigation can commit the edit. This is not loss of an acknowledged save or proof that every keyboard path fails.
Deactivated workflows demonstrate the issue; Claude also checked a never-activated Draft, so deactivation is not the cause. Claude-only Enter behavior remains outside joint scope.
No downstream execution damage is claimed. Newer source and the maintainer Tab fix support the source explanation; newer runtime was not tested.

bugs.expected: A completed Update Record action applies its saved No record choice by clearing the selected Person’s Company relation.
bugs.actual: The saved action contains companyId:null with Company selected for update. The run and step report success, but the output and refreshed Person retain the old Company. reproSteps: Create disposable Companies and People with existing Company links. Build a manual workflow with Update Record targeting one Person.
Select Company under Fields to update and choose No record in its picker. Close the editor, reload and confirm the saved choice.
Run the workflow and compare the Update Record result and refreshed Person’s Company with the requested clear.
Repeat for a fresh Person. Compare a non-null Company assignment and an ordinary record clear control.

UpdateRecordService calls removeUndefinedFromRecord before the write. The pinned helper uses isDefined and removes null as well as undefined, so the Company clear is absent from the submitted update.
